name: AI Energy Boom
description: Hypothesis scenario: no effective demand cap on energy — AI compute and robotics have near-unbounded appetite, and the binding constraint is financing, not saturation. Levers vs baseline: datacenter/robot ceilings lifted an order of magnitude (60,000 TWh / 3,000 per 1000 workers), AI cognitive payoff on (aiWorkerEquivalentPerTWh 1e5), endogenous energy-capex share (cleanShareFlex 1, up to 60% of investment). Since the unified financing ledger, robot fleets, energy buildout, and CDR all debit the SAME savings pool, so the financing constraint genuinely binds: WACC peaks ~15.6% around 2075 with K/Y compressed to ~1.8 before re-equilibrating (2026-model run: GDP 2100 ~$3,500T vs baseline ~$1,300T, generation ~740k TWh, warming ~2.7C). Sustained real rates >12% and K/Y <2 are outside anything observed — read the financing dynamics as qualitative. Uncalibrated hypothesis, not a forecast.
